commands.validate: Validate the HTML of every view

errors.bad_answer: The HTML validation could not read the answer of view {view}: {reason}
errors.bad_args: The HTML validation got arguments it cannot read: {reason}
errors.no_source: View {view} has no served source to validate: {reason}
errors.not_web: The page in view {view} is no web page to validate ({url}).
errors.nu_address_missing: The engine is the Nu HTML Checker, but no address is set in html-validate.nuAddress.
errors.nu_blocked: The page in view {view} did not let the request to the Nu HTML Checker at {address} through ({reason}): the page's Content-Security-Policy, mixed content or local network access rules can refuse it, or the checker allows no cross-origin requests. Validate this page with the built-in engine (html-validate.engine).
errors.nu_failed: The Nu HTML Checker at {address} failed for view {view}: {reason}
errors.project_rules: The project's rule file .rbrowser/htmlvalidate.json is invalid: {reason}
errors.too_large: The source of view {view} is {size} KiB, more than the {limit} KiB the HTML validation takes.

rules.area-alt: Image map areas have alternative text
rules.aria-label-misuse: aria-label only where the element can be named
rules.attribute-allowed-values: Attribute values are allowed for the element
rules.attribute-misuse: Attributes are used where they apply
rules.close-order: Elements are closed in the right order
rules.doctype-html: The doctype is the HTML doctype
rules.element-permitted-content: Elements hold only the content they permit
rules.element-permitted-occurrences: Elements occur no more often than permitted
rules.element-permitted-order: Child elements come in the required order
rules.element-permitted-parent: Elements sit in a parent that permits them
rules.map-id-name: Image map id and name match
rules.multiple-labeled-controls: A label names one control only
rules.no-dup-attr: No attribute is repeated on an element
rules.no-missing-references: References point to ids that exist
rules.no-multiple-main: At most one visible main element
rules.no-unknown-attributes: Attributes are known for their element
rules.script-element: Script elements have an end tag
rules.valid-for: label for attributes are valid ids

disabledRules.description: Rules the validation leaves out, by their id - for example no-raw-characters, or nu-info for the Nu checker's information messages.
disabledRules.help: html-validate's rules by their id, and nu-error, nu-warning and nu-info for the Nu HTML Checker's message types. A rule switched off here is never reported, whatever the findings' rule switches say.
disabledRules.label: Rules off

engine.description: Which validator checks the page source: html-validate, offline in rBrowser, or the Nu HTML Checker (the W3C validator) at the address below.
engine.help: html-validate runs offline on this device with a rule set close to HTML conformance. The Nu HTML Checker gives the W3C validator's own messages, but it needs an address - a local vnu, for example in a container.
engine.label: Validator

minSeverity.description: Messages below this severity are not reported.
minSeverity.help: Warning reports errors and warnings; error only errors; information also the Nu HTML Checker's information messages.
minSeverity.label: Lowest severity

nuAddress.description: The address of a Nu HTML Checker, for example http://localhost:8888/. The page source is sent there: with an address outside this device, the source of your pages leaves the device.
nuAddress.help: Used when the validator is the Nu HTML Checker. Only http and https addresses. A local vnu keeps the source on this device; https://validator.w3.org/nu/ sends the source of every validated page to the W3C. Empty by default, so nothing is sent anywhere.
nuAddress.label: Nu HTML Checker address

source.description: What is validated: the page source as the server sent it, or the DOM after rendering - what scripts built and what the browser made of the markup.
source.help: Source as served is what the W3C validator checks; its findings name a line and column. Rendered DOM validates the page as it is now; its findings name the element by selector, as the lines of a serialized DOM mean nothing. A project's .rbrowser/htmlvalidate.json sets rule levels and options in a trusted workspace.
source.label: Source

tools.validate: Validates the HTML of the page in the views - every view or the one of target - and answers the messages as findings with rule, place and the views and breakpoints each was found in. source raw (the default of html-validate.source) validates the page source as the server sent it, like the W3C validator, with line and column; rendered validates the DOM after rendering, with the element's selector. The engine is html-validate offline, or the Nu HTML Checker at html-validate.nuAddress when html-validate.engine is nu; engine and source override the settings for this call. A trusted project's .rbrowser/htmlvalidate.json sets rule levels and options; projectRules says whether it was applied.
